subject.title: [Feature]: REST endpoint for session management in HTTP API integrations

question: Should OpenClaw expose a narrow public `/v1/sessions/*` HTTP session-management API for OpenAI-compatible integrations, or should HTTP-only callers use the existing opt-in admin HTTP RPC/plugin and WebSocket control plane instead?
rationale: The requested behavior is technically grounded, but reset, compaction, model, and reasoning mutations over bearer-authenticated HTTP change the security and product boundary for third-party integrations.

options.title: Approve narrow `/v1/sessions/*` API
options.body: Implement focused reset/status/compact/model/reasoning endpoints with explicit operator-scope mapping, tests, docs, and no slash-command re-enablement.

options.title: Keep admin RPC as the HTTP control plane
options.body: Document `admin-http-rpc` as the supported trusted-host workaround and leave `/v1/chat/completions` focused on chat turns only.

options.title: Approve reset/status only first
options.body: Start with read/status plus reset as the common workflow and defer model/reasoning/compaction until the HTTP security model is proven.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow `/v1/sessions/*` API
recommendation.body: Implement focused reset/status/compact/model/reasoning endpoints with explicit operator-scope mapping, tests, docs, and no slash-command re-enablement.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` HTTP integration surface that vincentkoc recently added and documented.
